environment: Mathlib (lake env lean, Lean 4.30.0, Mathlib c5ea0035)

template_hole.type: {V : Type} → [Fintype V] → [DecidableEq V] → (G : SimpleGraph V) → [DecidableRel G.Adj] → Matrix V V ℕ
template_hole.description: corrected matrix criterion M(A, n) whose zero entries certify unreachability

allowed_edits.repair_object: a corrected matrix criterion M(A, n) and a kernel-checked proof of the corrected entrywise statement ∀ i j, (M) i j = 0 → ¬ G.Reachable i j (and, for the source's criterion, the iff with connectivity on a nonempty vertex type)
allowed_edits.may_change: only the matrix expression G.adjMatrix ℕ ^ (Fintype.card V - 1) (e.g. another polynomial or sum in A and n)
must_preserve: quantification over all finite simple graphs; matrices over ℕ
an explicit convention for the empty vertex type (Nonempty V may be assumed for the connectivity iff and must be stated)
allowed_edits.hypotheses_not_strengthenable: may not restrict to bipartite graphs, to specific n, or to diagonal/off-diagonal entries silently (the source's off-diagonal scope needs the narrower qualification and must be named)
allowed_edits.nonvacuity: the corrected criterion must give a nonzero (0,1) entry on the witness path graph and must not be the constant matrix
allowed_edits.not_allowed: keeping A^(n-1) and adding hypotheses; a criterion mentioning Reachable itself

hole_syntax.note: a matrix expression in G.adjMatrix ℕ and Fintype.card V; a criterion built from Reachable itself is the contract's not_allowed item and is excluded syntactically (harness passes it if the solver proves the obligations)

reference_repair: repair_entry_exact (line 202): ((1 + A)^(n-1)) i j ≠ 0 ↔ G.Reachable i j; repair (213): [Nonempty V] G.Connected ↔ ∀ i j, ((1 + A)^(n-1)) i j ≠ 0; repair_sum (240): the sum-of-powers variant
endpoint_statement: the source's own theorem (stored source line 0001) with the submitted criterion: ∀ V [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] (G) [DecidableRel G.Adj], G.Connected ↔ ∀ i j, criterion G i j ≠ 0 (= repair, line 213, for the reference criterion)
test_instances_source: reference (I + A)^(n-1) evaluated by decide +kernel; zero exactly at unreachable pairs (repair_entry_exact)

source_exposed_repair.where: stored answer line 0001: the source's THEOREM is `G is connected iff (I_n + A)^{n-1} has no 0s`, which is the corrected criterion itself (the package's `repair`, line 213); line 0007 explains the role of the identity; lines 0005, 0010, 0012 reason about (I+A)^{n-1}. The located line 0008 wrongly reasons about A^{n-1}.
source_exposed_repair.consequence: repair reconciliation / universal formalization task: the solver must prove the source's own (I+A)^{n-1} criterion universally and identify that A^{n-1} does not work; not hidden-repair discovery

task.title: Adjacency powers: which matrix certifies connectivity

located_defect.description: The source (stored source line 0008) argues that a zero entry of A^(n-1) means the two vertices are not connected by a path, so the graph is disconnected. Read over every finite simple graph (matrices over ℕ, entries counting walks) this entrywise statement is the located defect. Supply the corrected matrix criterion, prove the corrected entrywise statement for every finite simple graph, show the criterion is not constant, and prove the source's theorem (line 0001) with the corrected criterion: on a nonempty vertex set G is connected iff the criterion has no zero entry.

task.allowed_edit: Replace the hole in `criterion` by a matrix expression in G.adjMatrix ℕ and Fintype.card V (powers, sums, 1; no Reachable/Connected/Walk, no if/match); nothing else in the fixed part may change. The conclusions (¬ Reachable, ¬ Connected), the quantification over all finite simple graphs with matrices over ℕ, and the Nonempty V convention of the target theorem are fixed; graphs may not be restricted (bipartite, specific n, off-diagonal only). Do not redefine HasZeroEntry, LocalClaimEntrywise, LocalClaim, UniversalLocalClaim or UniversalLocalClaimEntrywise; no instances, notations, macros, axioms or exports.
task.challenged_passage: 0008 If any $A^{n-1}_{i,j}$ would be 0, that would mean that there would not be any path connecting those vertices. Thus, the graph would be disconnected.

notes: The final theorem is the source's own theorem (stated with the submitted criterion), per the contract's 'for the source's criterion, the iff with connectivity on a nonempty vertex type'.
Agreement instances test zero-ness (criterion G i j = 0 ↔ reference = 0), not the numerical entries, so the sum-of-powers criterion and any other exact criterion agree.
Nonvacuity names only ⊥ on Fin 2 (not the witness path graph); the witness P3 is checked only in AGREE.lean.
